titleZh: Robotti回归：英国公司Autonomous Agri Solutions接手，确保机器人未来
summaryZh: 丹麦农业机器人制造商Agrointelli破产六个月后，其Robotti自主田间机器人的硬件资产被英国Autonomous Agri Solutions (AAS)收购。AAS此前是Robotti在英国的官方销售和服务商，此次收购涵盖硬件、零部件和生产材料，但不包括已单独出售的知识产权和软件。文章分析了Robotti技术成熟但商业化失败的教训、对现有用户的影响以及AAS的背景和优势。
featuredReason: 本文揭示了农业机器人从技术成熟到商业落地的关键挑战——资本、分销与服务网络的规模化瓶颈，对智慧畜牧领域同样面临硬件与商业模式脱节问题的从业者具有重要借鉴意义。

Robotti is back: UK company Autonomous Agri Solutions steps in to secure the robot’s future

 02-09 | Field robots | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Agrointelli reached technical maturity but fell short on the capital, distribution, and service network needed to turn a working robot into a global business. Photo: Bush Organics

6 months after Danish manufacturer Agrointelli collapsed into bankruptcy, the Robotti autonomous field robot has found a new home. UK-based Autonomous Agri Solutions (AAS) has acquired the key hardware, machinery, parts, production materials, and technical assets needed to continue supporting the platform.

“Robotti is back – and ready for the future”, AAS announced on LinkedIn. “This is a major milestone for Autonomous Agri Solutions and the start of an exciting new chapter for Robotti”. For the growers who bought a Robotti – and for the wider agricultural robotics sector – it is a significant development.

Agrointelli filed for bankruptcy in late February 2026, after the Danish court determined the company lacked sufficient liquidity to continue operating. At the time, the company had delivered over 65 robots, which had clocked up more than 10,000 hours of operation in 20 countries. Future Farming reported the bankruptcy as it unfolded, noting that there would be no immediate consequences for current users, and that the company would continue to provide service and maintenance for sold models.

The company held 13 global patents and a proven fleet with more than 10,000 hours of commercial operation in fields across the globe. Photo: Bush OrganicsIntellectual property and software

The hope was that Agrointelli would be acquired as a going concern. Trustee Nicolai Thornemann said at the time: “The company is intact, all employees are on site with confirmed orders to produce. We are looking for a new owner who can continue the journey toward becoming the global market-leading autonomous platform.”

That outcome did not materialise. As a full sale of the company proved unsuccessful, only the intellectual property and software were sold – to companies within the sector, according to Danish trade publication Landbrugnet. According to the trustee, this solution generated the highest return. The buyers of the patents and software are reportedly industry players. All 20 employees were made redundant.

The acquisition by AAS – recently announced – is a separate transaction covering the physical assets: hardware, machinery, spare parts, production materials, and technical documentation. Whether AAS also holds or has access to the software and intellectual property sold separately in April remains unclear. Future Farming has requested comment from AAS and will update this article when a response is received.

The situation for customers outside the UK – in the Netherlands, Germany, Scandinavia, and beyond – is less certain, and will depend on whether existing regional distributors remain involved or whether AAS takes on direct responsibility. Photo: Mark PasveerWho is Autonomous Agri Solutions?

Autonomous Agri Solutions was founded by two Agricultural Engineering graduates with a passion to propel the UK into the so-called Fourth Agricultural Revolution. Both grew up on farms and worked across different agricultural enterprises throughout their careers. Tom Beach has worked for a handful of the largest fresh produce growers across the UK, while Jack Wyatt has more experience in the arable and livestock sector. Both are graduates of Harper Adams University, the UK’s leading agricultural university.

The two spotted the Robotti at Agritechnica in 2019 and immediately saw its potential. “The robot’s lightweight design and simplicity is what caught our eye the most”, they recall. “It is built from standard off-the-shelf components that are used throughout our industry in a wide range of machines. After the show, we realised the opportunity to bring Robotti to the UK and began talks with Agrointelli.”

AAS went on to become the UK’s official sales and service provider for Agrointelli Robotti – the natural starting point for a company now stepping in to secure the platform’s future. Their background gives them something that a purely financial acquirer would not have: hands-on field experience with the machine, an existing customer base in the UK, and established relationships with growers who rely on it.

Why the Robotti still has a future

The Robotti case was not a failure of technology, but of industrial scaling. Agrointelli reached technical maturity but fell short on the capital, distribution, and service network needed to turn a working robot into a global business. The company held 13 global patents and a proven fleet with more than 10,000 hours of commercial operation in fields across the globe. The product worked. The business model did not scale fast enough to sustain it.

For AAS, this distinction clearly matters. The platform they have acquired is technically validated – it has been used for seeding, mechanical weeding, hoeing, and band-spraying across multiple crops and countries. Plans had also been afoot to extend the machine’s weed control capabilities to include electrical and laser-based systems, for targeted control of larger weeds without soil disturbance. Whether those development roadmap ambitions survive the transition to new ownership is one of the key open questions.

The platform AAS has acquired is technically validated – it has been used for seeding, mechanical weeding, hoeing, and band-spraying across multiple crops and countries. Photo: Koos GroenewoldWhat this means for existing customers

The most pressing concern for growers currently operating a Robotti is continuity: will their machine keep working, will software updates continue, and who will service it? AAS has not yet published detailed answers to these questions, but their acquisition of spare parts, production materials, and technical assets suggests they intend to maintain service capability.

Their existing role as UK dealer means they already have service infrastructure in place domestically. The situation for customers outside the UK – in the Netherlands, Germany, Scandinavia, and beyond – is less certain, and will depend on whether existing regional distributors remain involved or whether AAS takes on direct responsibility.

The software question is arguably the most critical. The intellectual property and software were sold separately to unknown buyers within the sector. If AAS does not hold those rights, the long-term development of the Robotti platform – including software updates, autonomous navigation improvements, and new feature development – depends on whoever acquired the IP. That could mean a licensing arrangement, a partnership, or a gap in capability that AAS will need to address.

translationZh:
丹麦制造商Agrointelli破产六个月后，Robotti自主田间机器人找到了新家。总部位于英国的Autonomous Agri Solutions (AAS)已收购支持该平台继续运营所需的关键硬件、机械、零部件、生产材料和技术资产。

“Robotti回来了——并已为未来做好准备”，AAS在LinkedIn上宣布。“这是Autonomous Agri Solutions的一个重要里程碑，也是Robotti激动人心的新篇章的开始”。对于购买了Robotti的种植者——以及更广泛的农业机器人行业——这是一个重大进展。

Agrointelli于2026年2月下旬申请破产，此前丹麦法院认定该公司缺乏足够的流动性来继续运营。当时，该公司已交付超过65台机器人，在20个国家累计运行超过10,000小时。Future Farming在破产发生时进行了报道，指出对现有用户不会产生直接影响，公司将继续为已售型号提供服务和维护。

**知识产权和软件**

人们曾希望Agrointelli能作为持续经营企业被收购。受托人Nicolai Thornemann当时表示：“公司完好无损，所有员工都在岗，并有确认的订单需要生产。我们正在寻找一位新所有者，能够继续推动其成为全球领先的自主平台。”

这一结果并未实现。由于公司整体出售未能成功，只有知识产权和软件被出售——据丹麦行业刊物Landbrugnet报道，买家是业内公司。据受托人称，该方案产生了最高回报。专利和软件的买家据称是行业参与者。所有20名员工均被裁员。

AAS的收购——最近宣布——是一笔单独的交易，涵盖实物资产：硬件、机械、备件、生产材料和技术文档。AAS是否也持有或能够访问4月份单独出售的软件和知识产权仍不清楚。Future Farming已请求AAS发表评论，收到回复后将更新本文。

**谁是Autonomous Agri Solutions？**

Autonomous Agri Solutions由两位农业工程毕业生创立，他们热衷于推动英国进入所谓的第四次农业革命。两人都在农场长大，并在职业生涯中从事过不同的农业企业工作。Tom Beach曾在英国几家最大的鲜食生产商工作，而Jack Wyatt在耕地和畜牧领域拥有更多经验。两人均毕业于英国顶尖农业大学哈珀亚当斯大学。

两人在2019年Agritechnica展会上发现了Robotti，并立即看到了其潜力。“机器人的轻量化设计和简洁性最吸引我们”，他们回忆道。“它由我们行业在各种机械中广泛使用的标准现成组件构成。展会结束后，我们意识到将Robotti引入英国的机会，并开始与Agrointelli洽谈。”

AAS随后成为Agrointelli Robotti在英国的官方销售和服务提供商——对于一家现在介入以确保该平台未来的公司来说，这是一个自然的起点。他们的背景赋予了他们纯粹财务收购方所不具备的东西：对机器的亲身实地经验、在英国现有的客户群，以及与依赖该机器的种植者建立的稳固关系。

**为什么Robotti仍有未来**

Robotti的案例不是技术失败，而是产业规模化失败。Agrointelli达到了技术成熟度，但在将一台可用的机器人转变为全球业务所需的资本、分销和服务网络方面存在不足。该公司拥有13项全球专利，以及一支在全球田间拥有超过10,000小时商业运营经验的成熟车队。产品是可行的。但商业模式未能足够快地扩展以维持其运营。

对AAS而言，这一区别显然很重要。他们收购的平台已经过技术验证——它已在多个国家和多种作物上用于播种、机械除草、中耕和带状喷洒。此前还计划将该机器的除草能力扩展到电力和激光系统，以在不动土壤的情况下实现对大型杂草的靶向控制。这些发展路线图雄心能否在所有权过渡后幸存，是关键问题之一。

**这对现有客户意味着什么**

目前操作Robotti的种植者最紧迫的担忧是连续性：他们的机器能否继续工作，软件更新是否会继续，谁来提供维护服务？AAS尚未公布这些问题的详细答案，但他们收购备件、生产材料和技术资产表明他们打算维持服务能力。

他们作为英国经销商现有角色意味着他们已经在国内建立了服务基础设施。英国以外客户的情况——在荷兰、德国、斯堪的纳维亚及其他地区——则不太确定，这将取决于现有区域分销商是否继续参与，还是AAS直接承担责任。

软件问题可以说是最关键的。知识产权和软件已单独出售给业内未知买家。如果AAS不持有这些权利，Robotti平台的长期发展——包括软件更新、自主导航改进和新功能开发——将取决于谁获得了知识产权。这可能意味着许可安排、合作伙伴关系，或者AAS需要解决的 capability 缺口。
author: René Groeneveld
